mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two signed differences, keep the subtraction order exactly as written on both sides, i.e., interpret "(A - B) = (C - D)" literally, not as absolute values or swapped terms.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever you encounter a sentence of the form "The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "the number of potatoes that X has more than Y equals the difference between the number of potatoes that A and B have" as X - Y = B - A (swapped order) instead of X - Y = A - B.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: As soon as a variable’s exact numeric value is known, replace that variable with its value in all remaining equations and constraints, and propagate any resulting simplifications immediately.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After any step that yields a concrete number for a person’s count.
mathgap.example: Determining "Alice = 5" but leaving the equation "Bob - Alice = 3" unchanged, causing the system to remain unsolved.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement (e.g., "A has K more than B") using the current counts at the moment the statement appears, after all earlier transfers and overrides have been applied.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a comparative sentence in the narrative order.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "Bob has 3 more oranges than Alice" before applying a prior transfer that gave Alice additional oranges, thus using outdated counts.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the smallest set of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly linked to the queried person, and ignore all statements that involve unrelated variables.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after reading the query, before processing the full list of statements.
mathgap.example: Including equations about "Zoe" and "Yvonne" when the question only asks for "Bob’s" count, which adds unnecessary complexity and can cause errors.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat every capitalized token as a separate variable, even if two names differ by only a single character; never merge them unless the text explicitly says they refer to the same person.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a new name appears in the text.
mathgap.example: Assuming "Harve" and "Harvey" refer to the same person and using a single count for both.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret "the difference between the number of X that A and B have" as the signed subtraction A - B, preserving the order of the names as given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing sentences that mention "difference between … A and B".
mathgap.example: Translating "difference between A and B" as |A - B| or as B - A, which loses the intended sign.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Convert "A has K more (fewer) items than B" into the signed equation A - B = K (or A - B = ‑K for "fewer"), preserving direction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative phrase with "more" or "fewer" appears.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "A has 5 more items than B" as B - A = 5, swapping the direction.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement "X has N items" appears, assign X = N at that point, overwriting any previous value for X, and re‑evaluate any equations that involve X with the new value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a direct count sentence is encountered.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a later statement "Charlie has 7 oranges" that should replace an earlier "Charlie has 5 oranges".

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application (Bidirectional)
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer "X gives K items to Y" immediately when it appears, subtracting K from X and adding K to Y, using the current counts at that moment.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a transfer sentence in narrative order.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one, leading to incorrect intermediate counts.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Difference Equality Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements equating two signed differences, evaluate the equality using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after all prior transfers and overrides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a difference‑equality sentence while processing the text sequentially.
mathgap.example: Using pre‑transfer values to evaluate "(A - B) = (C - D)" after a transfer that changes A’s count has already occurred.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the order of subtraction, interpreting "A has K more than B" as B - A = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that "more" means A - B = K; enforce the signed direction consistently.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model interprets "difference between A and B" as |A - B|, discarding sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order and sign; interpret the phrase as A - B.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies all transfers after reading the whole text, rather than in the order they appear.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfers sequentially, updating counts immediately as each transfer statement is encountered.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes the first direct count is the true count and ignores later statements that should overwrite it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each direct count when encountered, overwriting any previous value for that person.

mathgap.description: Ignoring chronological order when evaluating difference equality statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model evaluates difference equalities using initial counts, not the updated counts after earlier statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Evaluate each difference equality at the moment it appears, using the current counts after all prior updates.
